decisions: VERIFIED, NOT JUST WRITTEN: I stood up a local PostgreSQL 16 instance, stubbed the prerequisites another agent owns (enums, has_role, update_updated_at_column, user_roles + its own-row RLS policy, finance_modules, auth.users, auth.uid()), applied this SQL clean, and ran the full acceptance matrix as anon / authenticated non-admin / admin. All pass. First run of my own test harness was itself buggy (set_config with is_local=true is discarded by psql autocommit, so auth.uid() was NULL for every role and the anon/non-admin denials were passing for the wrong reason); I caught it because the ADMIN cases failed, fixed it to session scope, and re-ran on a clean database.

content_json / layout_config: OMITTED. `grep -rn 'content_json|layout_config' src/` returns ZERO hits across all .ts/.tsx. Migration 20260212090000 that adds them was authored locally and never applied live, and types.ts does not declare them. Precedence rule 1 (actual usage wins) therefore excludes both. Note the near-miss: publishValidation.ts has a `contentJson` field, but it is a parsed in-memory TipTap JSONContent derived from the `content` text column, not a DB column - camelCase, never in a .select()/.insert().

REGRESSION TEST FOR FAILURE (a): I did not just avoid has_role - I reproduced the original outage condition. After the schema was up I ran `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.has_role(uuid, app_role) FROM anon, authenticated, PUBLIC` and re-ran every read and write. Anon reads of published essays, admin reads of drafts, admin UPDATE, and admin reads of admin_audit_log / council_sessions / books_uploads ALL still succeeded, with no 'permission denied for function has_role'. The inlined EXISTS makes the policies genuinely independent of the grant, not merely differently-worded.

REGRESSION TEST FOR FAILURE (b): anon SELECT returns only the published row; the draft row is absent both in a full table scan and in a targeted .eq('slug','draft-essay'). I also inserted a row with published = NULL and confirmed anon cannot see it - `USING (published = true)` is fail-closed on NULL, so a partially-written row does not leak.

essays.category_id is NOT NULL even though types.ts declares it `string | null`. types.ts is stale on this column: 20260215_001 ran `ALTER COLUMN category_id SET NOT NULL`, and docs/DECISIONS.md:77-81 states outright 'essays.category_id is NOT NULL with FK RESTRICT'. Same call on categories.section_id (NOT NULL, types.ts stale).

essays.module_id -> finance_modules ON DELETE RESTRICT (stated explicitly rather than left as the implicit NO ACTION the original migration got by omission). Evidence for the intent: 20260220_001_fix_production_finance_data.sql had to DELETE the dependent essays FIRST, commenting 'Remove those lessons first so the FK on essays.module_id does not block the curriculum rebuild' - the author hit the blocking FK and accepted it as correct behaviour rather than switching to SET NULL. RESTRICT also matches essays_category_id_fkey: content is never silently orphaned by a parent delete. Verified: deleting a module with a dependent essay errors.

idx_essays_slug is DELIBERATELY NOT recreated despite being on the carry-forward list. essays_slug_unique UNIQUE (slug) is a byte-identical (slug) b-tree that the planner uses for every slug equality lookup; a second non-unique index on the same single column costs write throughput and buffer cache for zero read benefit. Flagged here so you can override me if you want literal index-for-index parity.

The original UNIQUE (section, phase, slug) constraint on essays is dropped. essays_slug_unique is strictly stronger, and the composite enforces nothing whatever whenever phase IS NULL (NULLs are distinct in a unique index). The app already treats slug as globally unique - WriterEditor.tsx:167 'Slug is globally unique - no need to filter by section'.

FK constraint NAMES are load-bearing and preserved exactly: essays_category_id_fkey and categories_section_id_fkey are spelled out in PostgREST embed hints (useWriterEssay.ts:11 `categories!essays_category_id_fkey` nesting `sections!categories_section_id_fkey`; GreenTransitionPhase.tsx:142 `sections!categories_section_id_fkey`). Renaming either silently breaks Writer Studio and the green-transition phase page. Verified present in pg_constraint.

admin_audit_log is append-only: no UPDATE policy, no DELETE policy, and no UPDATE/DELETE grant to authenticated. An audit trail an admin can rewrite is not an audit trail. Verified: admin UPDATE and DELETE both fail with 'permission denied for table'. Insert also enforces user_id = auth.uid(), so an admin cannot forge an entry onto another user (verified: that insert is rejected).

Explicit per-table GRANTs instead of relying on Supabase's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES. RLS is only consulted AFTER the privilege check, so a table with perfect policies but no grant returns 'permission denied for table' from PostgREST. Being explicit also means anon is never granted any write privilege at all - a second independent barrier behind the 'no anon write policy' rule. Verified: anon INSERT on every table fails at the grant layer, before RLS is even reached.

Added CHECK (parent_id IS DISTINCT FROM id) on categories - a self-parent guard that was not in the live schema. The migration set was titled 'enforce_category_hierarchy' but never added it; no app code walks parent_id today, so a self-referencing row would be a latent trap for whatever eventually does. Low risk, but it IS a new constraint not present live - drop it if you want strict parity.

sections.voice_role stays text + CHECK rather than becoming voice_role_enum, even though the enum exists. types.ts types it as plain `string`; promoting it to the enum would change the generated TypeScript, which is outside a like-for-like baseline.
essays.date stays TEXT (not DATE). types.ts declares `date: string | null` and the original column is TEXT - it is a display string. Nothing in src/ orders or ranges on it.

council_sessions.post_id -> essays ON DELETE SET NULL, deliberately different from the RESTRICT used on essays' own parents: deleting an essay must not be blocked by its advisory history, and the transcript retains standalone value via input_snapshot. Verified: deleting the essay nulls post_id rather than erroring.

council_sessions.created_by NOT NULL DEFAULT auth.uid() is safe for the edge function specifically because supabase/functions/council-review/index.ts:87-89 builds its client from the publishable/anon key plus the caller's Authorization header - not the service_role key. auth.uid() therefore resolves to the signed-in admin. Had it used service_role, auth.uid() would be NULL and every insert would hit the NOT NULL. Verified: insert omitting created_by succeeds and lands the admin's uid; insert forging a different created_by is rejected by RLS.

useCreateEssay (src/hooks/queries/useAdminEssays.ts:185) builds a CreateEssayData payload with NO category_id, which would violate the NOT NULL. It is dead code - `grep -rn useCreateEssay src/` finds only its own definition, no call site. The live write paths (useSaveEssay in useWriterEssay.ts, and WriterEditor.tsx:314-322 which attaches category_id conditionally) are the ones that matter, and both send it. Not a reason to relax the constraint; worth deleting the dead hook separately.

Index set justified individually rather than copied: kept idx_essays_module_published + idx_essays_finance_section_published (20260301070510) and idx_essays_fsli_slug + idx_essays_topic (20260211100000, both partial since most rows are NULL). Added idx_essays_section_published_sort (useEssays' primary path: eq section [+ published] order sort_order), idx_essays_section_created (EditorialFeed / useRelatedEssays / GreenTransitionPhase fallback / DevelopmentFinancePhase, all eq section then order created_at DESC), idx_essays_category_id (eq/in on category_id AND the ON DELETE RESTRICT referencing-row scan, which would otherwise seq-scan essays on every category delete), idx_essays_updated_at (useAdminEssays + useUnifiedContent both order the whole table by updated_at DESC), and idx_essays_selected_published (partial, homepage useSelectedEssays).
open_risks: HARD DEPENDENCY on the user_roles agent's work, in two ways the inline-EXISTS pattern cannot self-satisfy: (1) `authenticated` must hold SELECT on public.user_roles - I restate this as a GRANT at the end of the file, but if their migration later REVOKEs it every admin check silently evaluates false and admins lose all write access; (2) user_roles RLS must contain a policy letting a user read their OWN rows (USING (auth.uid() = user_id)). The EXISTS subquery runs as the calling role, so user_roles' own RLS applies to it. If they ship user_roles with RLS enabled and admin-only SELECT, every admin check in this file breaks. This is the one failure mode the inline pattern trades for immunity to the has_role grant - please confirm against their output.

ORDERING: this SQL must be applied AFTER the migration that creates app_role / content_status_enum / lesson_type_enum, update_updated_at_column(), user_roles, and finance_modules. essays_module_id_fkey references public.finance_modules, so a finance_* agent's table must land before this file.

essays.published and essays.status can disagree in principle (published boolean vs the 4-value enum). RLS gates on `published`, but FinanceEssayPage.tsx:80 and EditorialFeed/GreenTransitionPhase gate the UI on `status = 'published'`. The app keeps them in sync (useSaveEssay sets published = (status === 'published')), but the tone trigger can flip status to 'tone_pending' independently. A row with published = true and status != 'published' would be RLS-visible to anon yet 404'd by the page. Pre-existing behaviour, not introduced here, but worth a follow-up: gate both on one column, or add a CHECK tying them together.

The tone trigger fires on the bulk-publish path too. useBulkPublish / useBulkPublishContent set status = 'draft' when unpublishing; if the essay has non-empty tone fields for its voice_role, validate_essay_tone_fields() rewrites status to 'tone_pending' rather than leaving it 'draft'. That is faithful to the live behaviour (verified: the promotion fires), but it means an unpublish does not always land on 'draft', and useUnifiedContent's status filter will bucket those rows under tone_pending.

books_uploads has no write path anywhere in src/ - the admin-only INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies are precautionary. If book uploads happen via a path I did not see (storage-triggered function, manual SQL, service_role script), confirm it runs as service_role or as an admin JWT, otherwise inserts will be denied.

CHECK (parent_id IS DISTINCT FROM id) on categories is a NEW constraint not present in the live schema. If the data re-import happens to contain a self-parented category row it will fail. Verified it rejects the self-parent case; drop the constraint if the import proves otherwise.

books_uploads.size_bytes is INTEGER (max ~2.1 GB), matching the live column and types.ts `number | null`. Fine for PDFs, but a larger asset would overflow. Left as-is for parity rather than widened to BIGINT.
